content: Darunavir increases the levels or effects of atazanavir by influencing the metabolism mediated by the hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4. The clinical significance of this interaction is currently unknown. Darunavir increases the levels or effects of bexarotene by influencing the metabolism mediated by the hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4. The clinical significance of this interaction is currently unknown. Darunavir increases the levels or effects of bosentan by influencing the metabolism mediated by the hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4. The clinical significance of this interaction is currently unknown. Darunavir increases the levels or effects of cevimeline by influencing the metabolism mediated by the hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4. The clinical significance of this interaction is currently unknown. Darunavir increases the levels or effects of clarithromycin by influencing the metabolism mediated by the hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4. The clinical significance of this interaction is currently unknown. Cyclophosphamide increases the levels or effects of darunavir by influencing the metabolism mediated by the hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4. Cyclophosphamide also increases the levels or effects of cobicistat by the same mechanism. The clinical significance of these interactions is currently unknown. Darunavir increases the levels or effects of dapsone by influencing the metabolism mediated by the hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4. The clinical significance of this interaction is currently unknown. Drospirenone increases the levels or effects of cobicistat by influencing the metabolism mediated by the hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4. The clinical significance of this interaction is currently unknown. Darunavir increases the levels or effects of docetaxel by influencing the metabolism mediated by the hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4. The clinical significance of this interaction is currently unknown. Darunavir increases the levels or effects of donepezil by influencing the metabolism mediated by the hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4. The clinical significance of this interaction is currently unknown. Drospirenone increases the levels or effects of darunavir by influencing the metabolism mediated by the hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4. The clinical significance of this interaction is currently unknown. Darunavir increases the levels or effects of dutasteride by influencing the metabolism mediated by the hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4. The clinical significance of this interaction is currently unknown. Darunavir increases the levels or effects of efavirenz by influencing the metabolism mediated by the hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4. The clinical significance of this interaction is currently unknown. Darunavir increases the levels or effects of eplerenone by influencing the metabolism mediated by the hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4. The clinical significance of this interaction is currently unknown. Darunavir increases the levels or effects of escitalopram by influencing the metabolism mediated by the hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4. The clinical significance of this interaction is currently unknown. When co-administering selective serotonin reuptake inhibitors (SSRIs), tricyclic antidepressants (TCAs), or trazodone with darunavir, dose titration of the antidepressant to achieve the desired effect may be necessary. It is recommended to use the lowest feasible initial or maintenance dose and monitor the antidepressant response closely. Darunavir increases the levels or effects of eucalyptus by influencing the metabolism mediated by the hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4. The clinical significance of this interaction is currently unknown. Darunavir increases the levels or effects of finasteride by influencing the metabolism mediated by the hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4. The clinical significance of this interaction is currently unknown. Cobicistat and ganaxolone interactions involve the hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical significance of these interactions is currently unknown. Changes in ganaxolone exposure when co-administered with strong, moderate, or weak CYP3A4 inhibitors are not expected to be clinically significant. Darunavir increases the levels or effects of imatinib by influencing the metabolism mediated by the hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4. The clinical significance of this interaction is currently unknown. Cobicistat and ixazomib interactions involve the hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical significance of these interactions is currently unknown. Clinical trials have shown that co-administration of ixazomib with strong CYP3A inhibitors does not result in a clinically meaningful change in systemic exposure to ixazomib. Darunavir increases the levels or effects of abemaciclib by influencing the metabolism mediated by the hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4. Strong CYP3A4 inhibitors increase plasma levels of abemaciclib and its metabolites, necessitating dose reduction. If a strong CYP3A inhibitor is discontinued, the abemaciclib dose should be increased after 3-5 half-lives of the inhibitor to the dose used prior to starting the inhibitor. Darunavir increases the levels or effects of acalabrutinib by influencing the metabolism mediated by the hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4. Co-administration with strong CYP3A inhibitors should be avoided. If a strong CYP3A inhibitor must be used short-term (e.g., up to 7 days), temporarily interrupt treatment with acalabrutinib. Darunavir decreases the effects of acarbose through pharmacodynamic antagonism. Use caution and monitor for new-onset or exacerbation of diabetes mellitus and hyperglycemia, which have been reported with protease inhibitors. Acetazolamide increases the levels or effects of cobicistat and darunavir by influencing the metabolism mediated by the hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4. The clinical significance of these interactions is currently unknown. Darunavir increases the levels or effects of adagrasib by influencing the metabolism mediated by the hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4. Co-administration with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors should be avoided until adagrasib concentrations have reached steady-state (~8 days). If steady-state is not reached, concomitant use of strong CYP3A4 inhibitors will increase adagrasib concentrations and the risk of toxicities. Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of ado-trastuzumab emtansine by influencing the metabolism mediated by the hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4. DM1, the cytotoxic component, is primarily metabolized by CYP3A4, and strong CYP3A4 inhibitors may increase DM1 exposure and toxicity. Darunavir increases the levels of afatinib by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Co-administration with P-gp inhibitors may require a reduction in the afatinib daily dose by 10 mg if not tolerated. Darunavir decreases the effects of albiglutide through mechanisms related to insulin resistance. Monitor closely for hyperglycemia, which has been reported with protease inhibitors. Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of alfentanil by influencing the metabolism mediated by the hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4. Clinical monitoring is recommended during co-administration with antiarrhythmics. Darunavir increases the levels or effects of amiodarone by influencing the metabolism mediated by the hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4. Clinical monitoring is recommended during co-administration with antiarrhythmics. Darunavir increases the levels or effects of amitriptyline by influencing the metabolism mediated by the hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4. Co-administration with SSRIs, TCAs, or trazodone may require dose titration of the antidepressant to achieve the desired effect. Use the lowest feasible initial or maintenance dose and monitor the antidepressant response closely. Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of amitriptyline by influencing the metabolism mediated by the hepatic enzyme CYP2D6. Carefully titrate the antidepressant dose to the desired effect, using the lowest feasible initial or maintenance dose, and monitor for antidepressant response. Darunavir increases the levels or effects of amlodipine by influencing the metabolism mediated by the hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4. Use caution and monitor closely. Amobarbital decreases the levels or effects of darunavir by influencing the metabolism mediated by the hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4. Use caution and monitor closely. Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of amoxapine by influencing the metabolism mediated by the hepatic enzyme CYP2D6. Carefully titrate the antidepressant dose to the desired effect, using the lowest feasible initial or maintenance dose, and monitor for antidepressant response. Anastrozole increases the levels or effects of darunavir and cobicistat by influencing the metabolism mediated by the hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4. The clinical significance of these interactions is currently unknown. Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of apalutamide by influencing the metabolism mediated by the hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4. Co-administration of apalutamide, a strong CYP3A4 inducer, with drugs that are CYP3A4 substrates can result in lower exposure to these medications. Avoid or substitute another drug for these medications when possible. Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of apixaban by influencing the metabolism mediated by the hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4. Avoid co-administration with strong dual inhibitors of CYP3A4 and P-gp. Darunavir increases the levels or effects of aprepitant by influencing the metabolism mediated by the hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4. Monitor closely. Darunavir increases the levels or effects of aripiprazole by influencing the metabolism mediated by the hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4. Reduce the aripiprazole dose by 25%, and by approximately 50% if administered with both a CYP3A4 inhibitor and a CYP2D6 inhibitor. Armodafinil decreases the levels or effects of darunavir by influencing the metabolism mediated by the hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4. Use caution and monitor closely. Cobicistat increases the levels or effects of armodafinil by influencing the metabolism mediated by the hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4. Avoid or use an alternative drug.
